Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 2–3 days of wheeze and exertional shortness of breath in a patient with prior asthma and atopy; suspected asthma exacerbation; advised increased short-acting bronchodilator via spacer, start antihistamine, prescribe spacer and peak flow meter, and arrange 1-week review with safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing and feeling short of breath.
- Onset/duration: 2–3 days.
- Course: Ongoing; patient currently feels “well” at rest but is breathless with walking; sometimes struggles to complete sentences.
- Associated symptoms: Cough without phlegm. Denies chest pain. Denies hemoptysis. No nocturnal awakenings. Reports “fever,” but measured temperature 37°C (normal).
- Functional impact: Unable to walk to work; working from home or on sick leave. Able to climb stairs.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Exercise worsens symptoms. No home peak flow monitoring.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): No chest pain, no hemoptysis, no sputum production, no nocturnal symptoms, no rest dyspnea at time of consult.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Childhood asthma; described as “quite bad,” required occasional hospital visits (no ICU).
  - Stopped regular medications “3–4 years ago” (patient-reported).
  - Current episode consistent with flare.
- Atopy: Hay fever; eczema.
- Medications related to PMH:
  - Salbutamol (albuterol) inhaler: patient reports “normally” taking it, approximately every few weeks; dose/route/frequency not documented. Conflict noted with statement of stopping asthma meds 3–4 years ago.
- Drug allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Engineer.
- Work status: Not walking to work due to symptoms; working from home or taking sick leave.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Patient-reported temperature 37°C (normal).
- No physical examination findings documented (telehealth).

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.
- Plan for home peak flow monitoring: record values morning and evening over the next week after pharmacist instruction.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute asthma exacerbation (possible triggers: seasonal allergens or viral infection)
  - Increase short-acting bronchodilator use: 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
  - Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate correct use.
  - Prescribe peak flow meter; monitor and record peak flows twice daily (AM/PM) for one week.
  - Safety-net: Call back immediately if high temperature develops or wheeze/shortness of breath worsens.
  - Arrange asthma review in ~1 week to assess control and consider adding controller therapy as needed.
- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
  - Start a regular over-the-counter antihistamine (per pharmacy advice; note in chart to guide choice).
- Issue 3: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
  - No active issues reported; no current treatment. Monitor.

General plan items:
- Pharmacist to provide education on spacer technique and peak flow use.
- Follow-up sooner if symptoms worsen before scheduled review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full medication reconciliation (names/doses/frequency), objective vitals (HR, RR, SpO2, BP), lung exam, baseline/previous peak flow or spirometry, inhaler technique assessment, vaccination status (e.g., influenza), asthma action plan.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Patient states they stopped asthma medication 3–4 years ago vs. also reports “normally” using salbutamol every few weeks (conflict noted).
  - Reports “fever” but measured temperature 37°C (normal) (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor ambiguities and brief communication lapses but clinically usable.
